link_training_waveforms.LT_LFPS: Low-Frequency Periodic Signaling ordered sets for link bring-up + lane bonding.
link_training_waveforms.sideband: SBU low-speed management pulses for connect/lane-config.

power_delivery_timing.CC_negotiation: USB Power Delivery message exchange on CC pins before high-power VBUS.

mdio_signal_timing.MDIO_TA_high_Z_window_clauses: Read transactions only; first TA bit must be high-Z on both ends, second TA bit driven 0 by PHY

frame_waveform.transmit: TX_EN ↑ on first preamble nibble → TXD shifts 7×0x55 + 0xD5 + DA + SA + Type/Length + Payload + Pad + FCS nibble-by-nibble → TX_EN ↓ on next TX_CLK after final FCS nibble → IFG (96 BT) before next TX_EN ↑.
frame_waveform.receive: PHY raises CRS as soon as line activity is detected → RX_DV ↑ aligned with first preamble nibble (or sometimes within the preamble) → RXD streams preamble + SFD + DA + ... + FCS → RX_DV ↓ before next RX_CLK after final FCS nibble → CRS ↓ shortly after.
frame_waveform.collision_half_duplex: (half-duplex only) During TX_EN, COL asserts as soon as the PHY detects a colliding signal; MAC immediately switches TXD to a 32-bit JAM pattern, then de-asserts TX_EN. After backoff slots, retry from TX_DEFER.

auto_negotiation_waveform.Acknowledge_propagation_pages: At least three identical Base Pages with Acknowledge bit set

transmitter_eye_reference_per_phy: MDI compliance eyes are specified per PMD clause: Figure 14-9 for 10BASE-T, Figure 25-? for 100BASE-TX, Figures 40-19..40-28 for 1000BASE-T. RJ-45 MDI return loss / NEXT specifications are also per PMD clause.
general_timing_rule: All MII / GMII signals are synchronous to TX_CLK (TX path) or RX_CLK (RX path); MDC is asynchronous. Bit times scale linearly with line rate (100 ns at 10 Mb/s, 10 ns at 100 Mb/s, 1 ns at 1 Gb/s); inter-frame gap = 96 BT and slot time = 512 BT (10/100 Mb/s) or 4096 BT (1 Gb/s) are both expressed in bit times so the same MAC FSM scales across the speed range.

line_code_waveform.transition: guaranteed transition at every bit boundary; mid-bit transition for logic 1
line_code_waveform.clock_recovery: receiver recovers clock from the BMC transitions

symbol_directionality.note: BMC is symmetric self-clocked coding; both link partners use the same 3.33 us UI / 1.67 us half-bit. No directional break/IBT asymmetry (each message is bounded by SOP* and EOP K-codes, not by an inter-byte gap), so the generic H0/H1/BR/IBT symbol set is not required on either side.

rx_timing.description: Host/external side - BMC symbols the PD engine RECEIVES (decodes) from the CC wire. The receiver recovers clock from the guaranteed BMC transitions.

logic0_full_ui_us.desc: logic 0 = one full BMC unit interval (single transition at the bit boundary, no mid-bit transition)

logic1_half_ui_us.desc: logic 1 = two half-UI cells (~1.67 us each) separated by an extra mid-bit transition

evidence.literal: USB-PD uses Biphase Mark Coding (BMC) on the CC wire at a nominal 300 kbaud. ... The unit interval (UI) is nominally 3.33 us.

tx_timing.description: DUT/internal side - BMC symbols the PD engine DRIVES onto the CC wire. The TX encoder must emit the same UI the partner's RX decoder tolerates.

logic0_full_ui_us.desc: drive one full BMC unit interval for logic 0 (boundary transition only)

logic1_half_ui_us.desc: drive two ~1.67 us half-UI cells for logic 1 (boundary transition plus mid-bit transition)

evidence.literal: BMC guarantees at least one transition per bit (a transition at every bit boundary, plus a mid-bit transition for a logic 1). ... The unit interval (UI) is nominally 3.33 us.
